intervals.label: cavity excavation
intervals.quote: Dec. 1991 The cavity excavation for the construction of the Super-Kamiokande detector started.

intervals.label: detector construction and water fill
intervals.quote: Jun. 1994 The cavity excavation was completed. The construction of the detector was started.

intervals.label: SK-I
intervals.quote: Super-Kamiokande began operation at midnight on April 1, 1996.

intervals.label: PMT implosion accident and recovery
intervals.note: History page: implosion accident Nov. 2001 damaged more than 6,777 inner-detector PMTs; recovery completed and observations restarted (at half photosensor density) in Oct. 2002.

intervals.label: SK-II (half PMT density after the 2001 accident)
intervals.quote: The observations restarted in October 2002 with half the original density of photosensors.

intervals.label: SK-III (full PMT density restored)
intervals.quote: Jun. 2006 Full reconstruction of Super-Kamiokande [...] the number of photomultiplier tubes in the inner tank is now 11,129

intervals.label: SK-IV (new front-end electronics and DAQ)
intervals.note: End date is when gadolinium loading (SK-Gd) began, per the same history page. A separate 2023 solar-neutrino paper (src:sk-prd-2024-solar) analyses an SK-IV data sample running only through May 2018; that is the cutoff of one specific analysis, not a stated end of the SK-IV hardware phase, so it is not used as the interval boundary.
intervals.quote: Replacement of front-end electronics and data acquisition system.

intervals.label: SK-Gd (gadolinium-loaded ultra-pure water)
intervals.quote: Aug. 2020 The SK-Gd Project Began With the addition of gadolinium, the upgraded Super-Kamiokande detector, known as SK-Gd, began operation.

name: Super-Kamiokande detector
notes: A detector-paper PMT count (NIM A 501, 2003) could not be extracted (PDF not machine-readable); the 11,129 figure is instead sourced from the official detector page, which is consistent with the 2026 INSPIRE experiment-record summary ('11,200 PMTs', an approximate paraphrase) and the SK-III restoration figure on the history page.

experiment_ids includes experiment:t2k and experiment:k2k in addition to experiment:super-kamiokande: this same physical detector serves as the far detector for both accelerator-neutrino programmes (K2K, 250 km from KEK; T2K, 295 km from J-PARC) as well as running its own solar/atmospheric/proton-decay/supernova physics programme. See src:t2k-nim-2011 ('...detected at the Super-Kamiokande...') and src:k2k-tutorial-page ('Neutrinos generated at KEK will be detected by the Super-kamiokande detector 250 km away.').

description.value: 11,129 inward-facing 20-inch (50 cm) PMTs covering about 40% of the wall, the world's largest PMTs at the time of installation.
1,885 outward-facing 8-inch PMTs used as a veto against incoming particles and for shielding characterisation.

description.quote: In June 2020, gadolinium was introduced to the ultra-pure water of the SK detector in order to detect neutrons more efficiently.
description.value: Gadolinium sulfate dissolved in the ultra-pure water from 2020 to tag neutron captures, improving sensitivity to inverse-beta-decay signals such as supernova relic neutrinos.

summary.plain: A cylindrical tank 39 metres across and 41 metres tall, filled with 50,000 tonnes of ultra-clean water and lined with more than eleven thousand light-sensing tubes, sitting a kilometre underground near Kamioka.
summary.technical: 39.3 m diameter x 41.4 m height stainless-steel tank; inner detector of 11,129 inward-facing 20-inch PMTs (~40% photocoverage), outer veto of 1,885 8-inch PMTs; 50 kt total / 22.5 kt fiducial mass. Rebuilt/upgraded through SK-I - SK-IV after a November 2001 PMT-implosion accident (full density restored June 2006); gadolinium-loaded since August 2020 (SK-Gd).

technology.quote: cylindrical stainless steel tank, which is 39.3 m in diameter and 41.4 m in height
technology.value: Cylindrical stainless-steel tank of ultra-pure water instrumented with inward- and outward-facing photomultiplier tubes, optically separated into an inner and an outer detector.
